name: Helblinghaus Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The Helblinghaus in Innsbruck's Altstadt: a 15th-century Late Gothic townhouse with a world-famous, opulent Rococo stucco facade created by Anton Gigl in 1732.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Helblinghaus (located at Herzog-Friedrich-Straße 10) is one of the most prominent architectural jewels of the historic Altstadt of Innsbruck. Situated directly opposite the world-famous Goldene Dachl at the junction with Pfarrgasse, this stately patrician house catches every eye with its spectacular facade. The exuberant, confectionery-like stucco decoration ranks among the finest and most masterly examples of civic Rococo in the entire Alpine region, forming a fascinating contrast to the adjacent Late Gothic buildings.

History & Facade Art

The architectural core of the Helblinghaus dates back to the Late Gothic period around the year 1480, when Innsbruck enjoyed an urban golden age under the Tyrolean territorial princes. Originally built as a typical Late Gothic town residence with bay windows and pointed-arch arcades for wealthy burghers, its facade remained austere for centuries. The house owes its present world-renowned splendor to the prince-episcopal court treasurer Johann Fischer, who purchased the property in 1725. Around 1730 to 1732, Fischer commissioned the Bavarian master plasterer Anton Gigl from the renowned artist dynasty of the Wessobrunner Schule to completely redesign the facade. Gigl enveloped the entire four-story gabled facade and both polygonal oriel bays in a dense, filigree network of white stucco marble against a delicate pastel pink background. Visitors can discover floral acanthus tendrils, bunches of grapes, fruit garlands, rocaille motifs, shell forms, mascarons, putti, and artfully entwined strapwork. The allegorical reliefs on the parapets of the bay windows are especially noteworthy. The building received its current name only in the 19th century after the innkeeper Sebastian Helbling, who owned the property from 1800 to 1827 and operated a popular wine tavern here. In 1980, the delicate stucco facade underwent a meticulous and comprehensive historic restoration.

Visit & Getting There

The splendid exterior facade of the Helblinghaus can be viewed and photographed from the outside in the pedestrianized Altstadt year-round and free of charge at any time. The building is privately owned; traditional retail shops and culinary establishments occupy the ground floor, while the upper floors are used as private residences. Arriving by public transport: From Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, walk in about ten minutes via Brixner Straße and Maria-Theresien-Straße directly into Herzog-Friedrich-Straße; tram lines 1 and 3 stop at the Marktplatz station (approx. a three-minute walk away). By car: Parking is available at the Altstadtgarage on Innrain or the Markthallengarage.

Tips

The entire pedestrian zone in front of the house is paved level and is accessible barrier-free for wheelchair users and strollers. The best time of day for detail shots of the intricate stucco work is morning or midday, when sunlight highlights the striking contrast between the white stucco and the pink background with sculptural clarity. Bring binoculars or a telephoto lens to admire the tiny faces, birds, and grapes nestled within the stucco ornament.
